stem:
Imran looks at two even numbers and asks when their sum is a multiple of 4.

Which two claims are correct?

options.text: The sum is a multiple of 4 when the two even numbers leave the same remainder on division by 4.
Every sum of two even numbers is a multiple of 4, with no further check.
One multiple of 4 plus one number of the form $4q+2$ gives a sum that is not a multiple of 4.
The same remainder rule also applies unchanged when one addend is odd.

teacher.key_rationale: Matching remainders mod 4 make an even+even sum a multiple of 4; mixed remainders (0 and 2) do not. Claiming every even sum works drops that check. Extending the rule to an odd addend over-scopes it.
